identity.title: daVinci-Dev: Agent-native Mid-training for Software Engineering

problem.claim: The paper examines how to adapt software-engineering models to dynamic, agentic deployment environments.

gap.claim: The authors state that post-training alone does not fully resolve the distribution mismatch between static pre-training and dynamic deployment.

contributions.claim: An agentic mid-training approach using agent-native data.
A two-part data formulation combining contextually-native trajectories for information-flow coverage and environmentally-native trajectories grounded in tool use and test execution.
Open-sourcing a substantial portion of the datasets, recipes, and model checkpoints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish agentic mid-training as a scalable complement to post-training and center it on agent-native data with contextual and environmental components.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their recipe outperforms Kimi-Dev on SWE-Bench Verified under two post-training settings, using the same base model and agentic scaffold, with fewer than half as many mid-training tokens: 73.1B.

The authors report state-of-the-art resolution rates among open agentic recipes using agentic scaffolds: 56.1% for the 32B model and 58.5% for the 72B model, despite non-coder Qwen2.5 starting models.
The authors also report gains on general code-generation and scientific benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Post-training is presented as insufficient for the mismatch between static pre-training and dynamic deployment.
The paper investigates scalable agentic mid-training as a complementary approach.
Agent-native data combines complete-information-flow trajectories with trajectories generated through actual tool invocations and test executions.
The recipe is reported to outperform Kimi-Dev, reach the stated open-recipe resolution rates, improve broader benchmarks, and release substantial research resources.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates agent-native data into contextual coverage/diversity and environmental interaction authenticity, then reports comparisons under matched base-model and scaffold conditions.

lessons.interpretation: Separating broad information-flow coverage from authentic interaction data can make a training-data argument more explanatory and its comparison more interpretable.
lessons.application: When proposing training data for tool-using agents, define distinct data roles and report comparisons while holding the base model and scaffold fixed.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the task has no meaningful tool interaction or when the data sources cannot be assigned distinct roles.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset composition, training procedure, statistical uncertainty, or per-setting results behind the reported comparisons.
The meaning of “state-of-the-art” is limited here to the described open agentic recipes using agentic scaffolds; the comparison set and evaluation protocol are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish why the reported gains occur or whether they generalize beyond the named benchmarks and model scales.
